title: Does Nike Have the Right Strategy Moving Forward? | NKE Stock Deep Dive Part 4
creator: Parkevtate Vosianc CFA
source_note: Detailed summary generated from video captions; auto-captions garble names/numbers in places. Video was members-only in earlier runs and went public before this run - Part 4 of the Nike deep dive.
summary: Part 4 of Parkevtate Vosianc's Nike deep dive - published to members earlier and released publicly before this run - asks whether Nike has the right strategy, and gives no buy, hold or sell verdict (the final verdict is reserved for the members-only Part 5). He focuses on the 'Pace' cost-cutting programme: roughly $2.5bn of savings targeted at about $1bn of restructuring cost (severance, contract settlements, lease exits), but most savings are not expected until fiscal 2029-30, with full realisation into fiscal 2031, and the turnaround timeline keeps extending, possibly into fiscal 2028. He questions whether Nike's business has become so large and stuck that a four-year restructuring is implausibly long compared with larger companies that have restructured faster, and is sceptical investors share management's confidence - while noting interest is rising with the stock near 52-week lows and valuation near multi-year lows. Prior tracked explicit Parkevtate NKE call remains HOLD (2 Oct); this part is UNCERTAIN, so no stance flip.
